verdicts.title: Compact SDPA sliding-window elision reopens OPQ-337: gemma2 with softcapping disabled attends to the full context
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced both claimed paths end to end on the current tree (transformers 5.15.1, torch 2.14, .venv/bin/python). (a) Tiny Gemma2ForCausalLM (hidden 64, 2 layers, layer_types=['sliding_attention','full_attention'], sliding_window=4, seq=12, _attn_implementation='sdpa', attention_mask=None): with attn_logit_softcapping=None upstream logits-sum = -2.3921028781624045 while opaque-patched = 11.014459269936197, which is bit-identical to the upstream no-window control (sliding_window=64 -> 11.014459269936197). With the default attn_logit_softcapping=50.0 patched matches upstream to 1e-6 (-2.3921039 vs -2.3921029). Scoping matches the claim exactly: with an all-ones attention_mask both give -2.3921028781624045, and with attn_implementation='eager' both give -2.3921039050037507. (b) Tiny MistralForCausalLM (sliding_window=4, seq=12, sdpa, attention_mask=None, attention_dropout=0.1, model.train() inside torch.no_grad(), apply_model_patches(..., dropout=False)): upstream 11.663893043994904 vs patched 11.734835026116343, and the upstream no-window control (sliding_window=64) is 11.734835026116343 - the window is fully dropped. With attention_dropout=0.0 the same pair agrees bit-for-bit (10.833540248917416), isolating the builder/forward predicate divergence. Code chain verified line by line: models/gemma2.py:35 installs masking_module_patcher=apply_compact_sdpa_sliding_window_masking_patch, which rebinds create_sliding_window_causal_mask to vmap_create_compact_sdpa_sliding_window_causal_mask (components/masking.py:29-40); that builder returns None when _can_use_compact_sdpa_sliding_window holds (runtime/masking.py:78-106, whose dropout clause is 'not torch.is_grad_enabled() or config.attention_dropout == 0.0'); vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2 (components/attention.py:670-738) reads sliding_window only inside 'if softcap is not None:' and otherwise returns vmap_sdpa_attention_forward(...) at :729, which has no sliding_window parameter and never applies a window (attention.py:169-241); vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_sliding_window (attention.py:169-199) requires runtime dropout == 0.0 and otherwise falls back to the same window-blind function. No guard, warning or assertion connects the two predicates. I looked for exits and found none: no attention_mask is required for the trigger (the HF default model(input_ids) shape), gemma2/mistral/ministral are the three families using the compact patcher, and the parity suite's _SLIDING_WINDOW_FAMILIES is only {'ministral','mistral'} with softcap unparametrized, so nothing pins gemma2's binding-window behavior. Not a duplicate of open #963 (that issue is purely performance: chunk-size tuning and padded-batch support for the compact path; it contains no correctness claim about the softcap=None fallthrough or the predicate divergence). Severity kept high but not critical: no privacy/epsilon effect, and each trigger needs one non-default knob (attn_logit_softcapping=None for gemma2; train()+no_grad with nonzero attention_dropout for mistral/ministral).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Two silent model-fidelity breaks, both requiring attn_implementation='sdpa' (the transformers default), attention_mask=None, no KV cache, and seq_len > sliding_window. (a) Gemma2 with attn_logit_softcapping explicitly set to None: every sliding-attention layer attends to the whole causal prefix instead of the window. Measured on a tiny 2-layer Gemma2 with sliding_window=4, seq=12: patched logits-sum 11.014459269936197 equals the no-window control exactly, while upstream gives -2.3921028781624045. With the default softcapping of 50.0 the patched path is correct. (b) Mistral/Ministral with attention_dropout != 0 evaluated in .train() under torch.no_grad(): the mask builder elides the window because grad is disabled while the patched SDPA forward declines to apply it because runtime dropout != 0, so the window is again lost (patched 11.734835026116343 == no-window control, upstream 11.663893043994904). Both paths are silent - no warning, no error - and neither affects accounting or epsilon. An all-ones attention_mask or attn_implementation='eager' avoids both.

verdicts.title: Parity suite still compares patched against patched for 21 of 26 families - sibling test modules re-contaminate what #812 restores
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced the whole chain. Collection order: 'pytest packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/models --collect-only -q' lists test_attention_impls, test_cohere, ..., test_olmo3, THEN test_parity.py and test_parity_harness.py, THEN test_phi3, test_qwen2, test_qwen3, test_qwen3_5_moe, test_qwen3_moe, test_qwen3_next, test_smollm3 - i.e. 5 of the families parametrized in test_parity have their own module collected after it. Per-family modules do apply patches with no restore (e.g. packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/models/test_llama.py:33 calls apply_model_patches(model, eager_attention=True) inside the tiny_model fixture), and parity_model_patches (_test_utils.py:266-300) snapshots _FAMILY_MODULE_PATCH_NAMES + ALL_ATTENTION_FUNCTIONS at context ENTRY, so an already-patched modeling module is recorded as the 'original'. Injected-regression proof: a pytest plugin that wraps opaque.api.patches.transformers.components.attention._grouped_eager_attention with a 5% scaling error gives (i) 'pytest test_parity.py -k eager-llama -p corrupt_plugin' -> 1 failed ('llama [eager] forward parity failed'); (ii) 'pytest test_llama.py test_parity.py -k "eager-llama or (llama and vmap)" -p corrupt_plugin' -> 4 passed; (iii) the whole models directory with the same injection -> 5 failed, 204 passed, 15 skipped, and the only failures are test_forward_logits_parity[eager-{phi3,qwen2,qwen3,qwen3_moe,smollm3}] - exactly the families whose module sorts after test_parity.py. So a real numerical regression in the shared eager-attention helper is invisible for the other families. Not a duplicate of an open issue: the contamination issue (OPQ-338 / #812) is closed, and the open child #813 covers the pytest.skip/xfail exemptions and the gpt2 gradient mismatch, not reference contamination. Severity medium is right - this is test evidence quality, not a shipped defect; it neither changes runtime behavior nor epsilon, but it does mean the parity evidence cited for the other patches fixes in this milestone is weaker than it appears.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Running the patches model test directory in one process (the CI lane), pytest collects 21 of the 26 per-family modules before test_parity.py; each has already rebound eager_attention_forward, repeat_kv and the mask builders in the family's modeling module with no restore, so build_patched_model_pair's 'unpatched' reference runs opaque's own implementations. Demonstrated by injecting a 5% scaling error into _grouped_eager_attention: the directory run reports only 5 failures (phi3, qwen2, qwen3, qwen3_moe, smollm3 - the families collected after test_parity.py) out of the 26 parametrized families, and the llama case that fails when test_parity.py runs alone passes once test_llama.py is collected with it. Consequence is lost regression detection in the parity suite only; no runtime or privacy impact.

verdicts.title: Gemma3 bidirectional attention: or_mask_function / and_mask_function are accepted and silently ignored by opaque's mask builders
verdicts.reasoning: Verified in code and by execution. vmap_create_causal_mask declares or_mask_function/and_mask_function at runtime/masking.py:165-166 and no line in its body (masking.py:186-315) references either name (checked with a scoped grep over the function's line range). vmap_create_sliding_window_causal_mask forwards both down to it at masking.py:388-389, and its SDPA short-circuit at masking.py:359-372 returns _sdpa_sliding_window_mask(...) or None without consulting or_mask_function, and_mask_function or block_sequence_ids - in contrast to _can_use_compact_sdpa_sliding_window (masking.py:96-101), which does check all three. Upstream usage confirmed in the installed transformers 5.15.1: modeling_gemma3.py:547-549 sets mask_kwargs['or_mask_function'] (constant True) and sliding_mask_kwargs['or_mask_function'] = _bidirectional_window_overlay(...) when config.use_bidirectional_attention, and :748-752 passes or_mask_function=blockwise_overlay(...) plus and_mask_function=sliding_window_overlay(...) for token-type/packed inputs. Reproduced on a tiny Gemma3ForCausalLM (Gemma3TextConfig, hidden 64, 2 layers, layer_types=['sliding_attention','full_attention'], sliding_window=4, seq=12, all-ones attention_mask): with use_bidirectional_attention=True, eager gives upstream 4.555333267260721 vs patched -3.7555809930818214, and sdpa gives upstream 4.555332317031571 vs patched -1.4175027664750814; with use_bidirectional_attention=False both agree exactly (-2.5061021458823234). No warning or error is emitted, and grep confirms no parity test sets use_bidirectional_attention. Downgraded from the 'same as OPQ-337' framing only in reachability: the flag is non-default (it is the EmbeddingGemma-style configuration) and the block_sequence_ids overlay belongs to the multimodal/packed path, which opaque's text-first support does not advertise; medium is the right severity for a silent architecture mismatch behind a non-default flag with no epsilon effect.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A Gemma3 text model configured with use_bidirectional_attention=True (the EmbeddingGemma-style setting) and patched via opaque.patches.apply_model_patches silently runs plain causal (and causal-windowed) attention, because opaque's vmap_create_causal_mask accepts or_mask_function/and_mask_function and never applies them and the sliding-window builder's SDPA short-circuit does not even check for them. Measured on a tiny 2-layer Gemma3ForCausalLM (sliding_window=4, seq=12, all-ones mask): logits-sum upstream 4.5553 vs patched -3.7556 (eager) and -1.4175 (sdpa); with the flag off the two agree bit-for-bit. The same silent drop applies to block_sequence_ids-driven blockwise/sliding overlays, which are absorbed by **kwargs. No warning is emitted and no parity case sets the flag. Privacy/accounting are unaffected; the harm is training or evaluating a different architecture than the config specifies.

verdicts.title: Fail-closed guard for unregistered HF families does not see PEFT-wrapped models
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced exactly on transformers 5.15.1 / peft 0.20.0. _is_hf_pretrained_model (_router.py:50-56) is isinstance(model, transformers.PreTrainedModel); the fail-closed raise at _router.py:133-142 fires only when that is True (with compat) or when dropout/batchify were passed explicitly True; the early 'return' at :149 precedes both the disable_dropout block (:164-168) and the PeftModel batchify block (:170-182). Execution: supported_families() has no 'falcon'; bare FalconForCausalLM -> ConfigurationError "opaque: compatibility/dropout/batchify patches require a registered transformers family; got 'falcon' (FalconForCausalLM)"; peft.get_peft_model(FalconForCausalLM(cfg), LoraConfig(target_modules=['query_key_value'])) gives isinstance(pm, peft.PeftModel)=True, isinstance(pm, transformers.PreTrainedModel)=False, detect_family(pm)='falcon', and apply_model_patches(pm) raises nothing - only WARNING 'opaque: no registered apply function for model family falcon; no model-level patches applied.' After the call the model still carries ('base_model.model.transformer.h.0.self_attention.attention_dropout', 0.3) and config.attention_dropout/hidden_dropout = 0.3. Checked the DPTrainer call site: _dp_trainer.py:844-850 passes compat/performance/kernels but not dropout or batchify explicitly, so the explicit-kwarg arm of the guard does not rescue it. Checked for a pinning test: packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/test_public_factory.py:671-690 and opaque-transformers' test_compile_and_kernel_args.py:74 only use bare PreTrainedModel subclasses; no test wraps an unregistered family in PEFT. Also verified the failure is not loud downstream: torch.vmap(torch.func.grad(...), randomness='same') over functional_call on the unpatched falcon+LoRA model in .train() runs without error, so dropout-active per-example gradients are produced rather than a crash. Severity medium, not high: a WARNING is logged, the family must be unregistered, and clipping still bounds sensitivity so epsilon is untouched.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: DP-fine-tuning a LoRA adapter over an unregistered Hugging Face family (verified with falcon) through apply_model_patches / DPTrainer: because peft.PeftModel is not a transformers.PreTrainedModel, the fail-closed guard added for unregistered HF models does not fire, and the router takes the warn-and-return branch even though detect_family() correctly resolves 'falcon'. Two vmap-safety steps are skipped along with the family patches: disable_dropout and the PeftModel batchify shim. Verified after the call that the attention dropout module still has p=0.3 and config.attention_dropout=0.3, and that vmap(grad(...)) with randomness='same' then runs without error, so every example in the microbatch shares one dropout mask and the per-example gradients differ from both ordinary training and the dropout-free configuration the trainer documents. The only signal is a WARNING log. Privacy is unaffected - clipping still bounds per-record sensitivity.
